claim: In the storage decision guide the Offline row is suitable for one-time or periodic uploads when data can be static in transit, makes sense when you need to use only the minimum available bandwidth and prefer the predictability of physical moves, and names AWS Data Transfer Terminal. The same guide says AWS will discontinue support for AWS Snowball devices in all AWS commercial Regions on 2026-12-31.

evidence.quote: |  Offline  | Suitable for one-time or periodic uploads - and when data can be static in transit. |  This choice makes sense when you need to use only the minimum available bandwidth - and you prefer the predictability of physical moves.   |  [AWS Data Transfer Terminal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datatransferterminal/latest/userguide/what-is-dtt.html) The Snow Family remains available to existing customers only.  |
evidence.table_header: | Migration options | When speed is the priority | When bandwidth is important | Storage services or tools |

evidence.quote: AWS will discontinue support for AWS Snowball devices in all AWS commercial Regions on December 31, 2026. This does not affect AWS GovCloud (US) customers with active Snow jobs.
